chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Stand in the left side of the mountain, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood at Arafat in the left side of the mountain. So when he stood, the people rushed to the heels of his camel and stood beside him. So he moved it nearby, so they did the same. Then he said: 'O people! The place of the heels of my camel is not the Station (Mawqif), but all of this is the Station,' and he gestured with his hand to the Station. And he did the same in Al-Muzdalifa.
So whenever you see a gap, fill it with yourself and your mount, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves that those gaps be filled. And move from the plateaus and avoid the Arak bushes.

So when you stand at Arafat, praise Allah, extol His holiness, glorify Him, laud Him, and proclaim His Greatness with one hundred Takbirs. And recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times, and choose for yourself from supplications whatever you like, and strive, for it is a day of supplication and asking.

And seek refuge with Allah from Satan, for Satan will not astound you in a place more beloved to him than to astound you in that place. And beware of being occupied with looking at the people, and turn your attention towards yourself.
Let what you say be: 'O Allah, Lord of all the Stations, free my neck from the Fire, expand for me from the Halal sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the mischievous among Jinn and humans.'

O Allah, do not plot against me, nor deceive me, nor drag me down. O Most Hearing of the hearers, and O Most Seeing of the seers, and O Quickest of the Reckoners, and O Most Merciful of the merciful! I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to do for me such and such.

Let what you say, while you are raising your hands to the sky, be: 'O Allah, my need which, if You grant it, what You withhold from me will not harm me; and if You withhold it, what You give me will not benefit me. I ask You for the liberation of my neck from the Fire.'
O Allah, I am Your servant, and a possession of Your Hand, and my forelock is in Your Hand, and my term is in Your Knowledge.

I ask You to enable me to do that which pleases You about me, and to accept from me my rituals which You showed to Ibrahim, Your Friend, and pointed to by Your Beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
Let what you say be: 'O Allah, make me from those whose deeds You pleased, and prolonged their lifespan, and revived them after death with a goodly life.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Surah 112)
key_terms.مَيْسَرَةِ الْجَبَلِ: The left side of the mountain

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and etiquettes for the Day of Arafat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the entire plain of Arafat constitutes the valid standing place (Mawqif), correcting the misconception that only the spot where the Prophet’s camel stood is sacred, thereby emphasizing the inclusivity of the ritual. The narration provides a structured liturgy for the Day of Standing, combining specific dhikr, self-reflection, and comprehensive du'a for liberation from Hellfire and acceptance of Hajj, rooted in the Prophet’s precedent. This guidance underscores the spiritual significance of Arafat as a time of divine acceptance and personal accountability, integral to Shia jurisprudence of the Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, fom Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Pause by the left of the mountain, for Rasool-Allahsaww paused by the left of the mountain.

So when he<sup>saww</sup> paused, the people came over encircling sandals by his<sup>saww</sup> camel, and they were pausing by his<sup>saww</sup> side. So he<sup>saww</sup> moved it nearby, so but they did similar to that. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people! The place of my<sup>saww</sup> camel is not for the sandals, being the Pausing Station, but this here, all of it is a Pausing Station’, and he<sup>saww</sup> gestured by his<sup>saww</sup> hand to the Pausing Station. And he<sup>saww</sup> did similar to that in Al-Muzdalifa.

So whenever you see a vacant spot, then close it (occupy) with yourself and your ride, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves that you should close up (occupy) that vacant spot, and transfer from the plateau, and fear Al-Arak.

So when you pause at Arafaat, then Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extol His<sup>azwj</sup> Holiness, and Glorify Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Laud (Extol) upon Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Exclaim His<sup>azwj</sup> Greatness with one hundred exclamations, and recite ‘Say He<sup>azwj</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is One (Chapter 112), and Al-Hamd (Chapter 1), one hundred times, and choose for yourself from the supplications whatever you like, and strive, for it is a day of supplication and asking.

And you should seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Satan<sup>la</sup> would never astound you in a place more beloved to him<sup>la</sup> than for him<sup>la</sup> to astound you in that place. And beware of being pre-occupied with looking at the people, and turn your attention towards yourself, and let yourself become in what you should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord of the Easts, all of them!

Free my neck from the Fire, and Expand upon me from the Permissible sustenance, and Turn around the evil from me, the mischief of the Jinn and humans. 
O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

Do not let me be plotted against, nor deceived, nor be dragged down. O most Hearing of the hearing ones, and O most Seeing of the seeing ones, and O Quickest of the Reckoners, and O most Merciful of the merciful ones! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Deal with me such and such.

And let yourself become in what you should be saying, and you are raising your hand towards the sky, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! My needs which, if You<sup>azwj</sup> were to Grant me it would not harm me what You<sup>azwj</sup> Prevent from me; and if Your<sup>azwj</sup> were to Prevent these, it would not benefit me what You<sup>azwj</sup> Give me. I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> to Liberate my neck from the Fire.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant, and a possession of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Hand, and my forelock is in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Hand, and my term is in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge.

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Incline me to whatever Pleases You<sup>azwj</sup> about me, and that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Accept my rituals from me which were shown by Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> Your<sup>azwj</sup> Friend, and were pointed to by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Beloved Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.

And let yourself become in what you should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make me to be from the ones whose deeds have Pleased You<sup>azwj</sup>, and Prolong my life-span, and Revive me after the death with a goodly life’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said

that you should stay toward the left side of the hill; the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, stayed on the left side of the hill in ‘Arafat. When he stopped, people then began to move close to him on the footsteps of his camel to stand next to him. He moved his camel and so also did the people, and he then said, ‘O people, the place to stay here is not limited to where my camel has set foot. In fact, this entire place is for staying;’ he pointed with his hand toward the whole area. He did the same thing in al-Muzdalifah.

‘If you find a vacant space, fill it up with yourself and transporting animal. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, loves that all of these places be filled up. Move away from the hillside and al-Arak.’

When you stay in ‘Arafat then praise Allah, speak of His Lordship, glory and praise. Say Takhir (Allah is great beyond description) one hundred times. Read Chapter 112 of the Holy Quran one hundred times. Choose for yourself whatever prayers you like. Strive hard; it is the day for prayer and appeal for help (before Allah).
Seek protection with Allah against Satan; Satan does not become tired in a place where he loves to make you feel tired (of praying). You should avoid looking at people. Come to yourself,

and of the things you say should be this, “O Allah, Lord of all of al-Mash’a‘ir (things that remind one of Allah), set me free of hellfire, increase my sustenance of the lawful kind and keep away from me the wickedness of sinful Jinn and man.

O Allah, do not plan against me, or prepare slippery conditions and do not lead me gradually to destruction. You listen to appeals better than all of those who listen. You are the best observer of those who observe, the swiftest of those who prepare accounts and the best of those who grant mercy. I appeal before You O Allah, to grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause), make so and so of my wishes to come true.”

Of the prayer you may say should be this when you raise your hands to the sky, “O Allah, my wishes are such ones that if You grant them, whatever You deny will not harm me and if You deny whatever You have granted me will not benefit me. I appeal before You to set me free from hellfire.
O Allah, I am Your servant, of the things that You own and the control of my forehead is in Your hand, and You know the time of my death.

I appeal before You to grant me the opportunity to do whatever pleases You with me. Accept the acts of my al-Hajj that I have performed following the instructions that you had given to Ibrahim Your friend and have showed them to Your beloved one, Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.”
In your prayers you should include this, “O Allah, make me of those with whose deeds You are happy, who are granted long life, and a beautiful life after death.’””
